### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, about 99 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions went to A27; in the later window this flow is split almost evenly over A35, A36 and A41 (about one third each), with A27 keeping under 1 in 100. Both profiles rest on about 200 traces. [DIR001]
- In the earlier window, A26's outgoing transitions went mainly to A41 (about 37 in 100), A35 (about 34) and A36 (about 28); in the later window, about 99 in 100 go to A30, again on about 200 traces per window. [DIR002]
- Each of A35, A36 and A41 sent roughly 28–37 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A30 and almost none to A27 in the earlier window; in the later window each sends about 31–34 in 100 to A27 and about 0.5 in 100 to A30, while transitions among the three activities themselves continue at similar shares in both windows. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- A35, A36 and A41 each occur earlier within traces in the later window (mean relative position about 0.58–0.59 before versus about 0.41 after), while A27 (about 0.38 to 0.47) and A26 (about 0.53 to 0.62) occur later; every one of these activities still appears in essentially all traces of both windows. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- A27 immediately followed A25 in about 99 in 100 earlier traces but lies about four steps after A25 in about 93 in 100 later traces; A30 followed A26 about four steps later in about 93 in 100 earlier traces but immediately in about 98 in 100 later traces. [LAG001, LAG003]
- Consistently, the pairs A26–A35, A26–A36, A26–A41, A35–A30, A36–A30 and A41–A30 occur within five steps in about 200 earlier traces but only 1–2 later traces, while the pairs A25–A35 and A35–A27 appear in about 199 later traces against 1 earlier trace; the thin side of each of these counts makes them indicative only. [LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A27 and the group A35/A36/A41 exchanged their order between A25 and A26: in the earlier window the flow ran from A25 to A27, then reached A26, then the group A35/A36/A41, with A30 following about four steps after A26; in the later window A25 leads into the group, the group leads to A27 within one to three steps, and A26 leads directly to A30. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG003, LAG007]

The support is direct and consistent: the successor profiles of A25, A26 and all three group members flipped in matching directions on about 200 observations per window, the two lag items with full support show the A25–A27 and A26–A30 distances changing from one to four steps and from four to one step, and the position shifts move the group earlier while A27 and A26 move later; every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, and 20 qualifying items against roughly 0.6 expected by chance for 120 tested units means the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. Because every involved activity occurs in essentially all traces of both windows, this is a reordering of existing activities, not activities being added, removed or skipped. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, LAG001, LAG003]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show whether A27 now always precedes A26 in every later trace, since no relational item covers that pair, and it cannot distinguish a single sequential segment from alternative branches after A25, because each of A35, A36 and A41 still leads to the others in both windows; several lag items also rest on only 1–2 observations in one window. [LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
